title: PowerPoint for Windows: create a presentation with Copilot from PowerPoint Home
summary: The rollout, default and licensing statements agree with Microsoft's notice and documentation. Both governance controls are documented, including the registry setting; minor corrections would complete the Cloud Policy route, retain the app-version qualification and add supporting references.

claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot presents only data that each individual can access using the same underlying controls for data access used in other Microsoft 365 services.

claims.claim: Prompts and responses receive Enterprise Data Protection when users sign in with Microsoft Entra accounts.
claims.quote: Copilot Chat (Basic), Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic), and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) are protected by Enterprise Data Protection (EDP) when you sign in with Microsoft Entra accounts.

claims.claim: Copilot produces a presentation draft for the user to review and refine.

claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Home create presentation Copilot Basic license; Copilot PowerPoint Windows Home create presentation Basic Premium license. Read overview, licence options, July 2025 and August 2026 release-note excerpts, support creation page; Basic Home wording found only for web.

claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Home create presentation Copilot Basic license separate price meter policy hide entry point; PowerPoint Home Copilot separate price meter spending control policy entry point Windows. Read licence options, overview, support creation page and usage-based billing overview.

claims.claim: No meter specific to the Windows PowerPoint Home entry point is published.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Home Copilot separate price meter spending control policy entry point Windows. Read licence options, Copilot overview, support creation page and usage-based billing overview; no Home-specific meter stated.

claims.claim: No spending control specific to this entry point is published.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Home Copilot separate price meter spending control policy entry point Windows. Read privacy controls, Cloud Policy, Copilot overview and usage-based billing overview; general controls are documented, no Home-specific spending control found.

claims.claim: The connected-experiences setting is reached through Customization > Policy Management > Create > Choose the scope > Configure Settings in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. ... select Create. ... On the Start with the basics page ... On the Choose the scope page ... On the Configure Settings page, select the policies
claims.fix: Use 'Customization > Policy Management > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content'. The cited privacy-controls page documents the final setting; the already-cited Cloud Policy overview documents the route.

claims.claim: Setting usercontentdisabled to DWORD 2 under HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\common\privacy disables content-analyzing connected experiences.
claims.quote: Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content | UserContentDisabled | 1=Enabled 2=Disabled ... [HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\common\privacy]

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Scope: Prerequisite; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Turning off content-analyzing connected experiences makes Copilot unavailable in PowerPoint on Windows, Mac, iOS and Android, including this Windows entry point.
claims.quote: If you turn off connected experiences that analyze your content ... Microsoft Copilot features won't be available ... PowerPoint ... This applies to when you're running the most current version of these apps on Windows, Mac, iOS, or Android devices.
claims.fix: In Scope, replace the prerequisite sentence with 'Microsoft's privacy page says that if connected experiences that analyze content are turned off, Copilot features are not available in the most current version of PowerPoint on Windows, Mac, iOS or Android.'

claims.claim: The analyze-content policy affects all connected experiences in that category, not only Copilot.
claims.quote: You can use the Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content policy setting to control whether these types of connected experiences are available to your users.

claims.claim: Office Apps Administrator is the recommended role for Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: Office Apps Administrator (Recommended) | This role can manage Office apps cloud services, including policy and settings management

claims.claim: A user's licence assignment is managed at Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: go to the Users > Active users page. ... Select the row of the user ... select Licenses and Apps. ... Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns the specified licence to the user.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Licence assignment requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: Removing the Microsoft Copilot licence removes the add-on experience rather than only the PowerPoint Home entry point.
claims.quote: Copilot is only available to users with a license assigned. If you remove the license from a user, the user loses access to Copilot.

claims.claim: Basic users retain the in-app Copilot capabilities described by the overview without an add-on licence.
claims.quote: You don't have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license but can use Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy settings normally apply when Office apps restart.
claims.quote: Policies from Cloud Policy are applied only when the Office app is restarted.

claims.claim: Some privacy policies apply without restarting Office apps.
claims.quote: Some policies related to privacy controls will apply without restarting any Office apps.

claims.claim: The Cloud Policy overview says Cloud Policy takes precedence over Group Policy on Windows Server.
claims.quote: policy settings implemented by using Cloud Policy take precedence over policy settings implemented by using Group Policy on Windows Server

claims.claim: The sensitive-and-regulated guidance says Group Policy takes precedence for Win32 Office apps when both policy mechanisms are in use.
claims.quote: Rich client Office applications (Win32 apps) are controlled by both Group Policy and Cloud Policy, with Group Policy taking precedence where both are in use.

claims.claim: Microsoft's sensitive-and-regulated guidance advises keeping Group Policy and Cloud Policy aligned.
claims.quote: For organizations that use a combination of Group Policy and Cloud Policy, keep these policies aligned to avoid confusion.

claims.claim: MC1311974 names no separate switch for the PowerPoint Home option.
claims.quote: Existing Microsoft 365 and Copilot policies are respected; no admin configuration changes are required. ... No action is required.
